entries.claim: This dependent same-recension digital comparison supplies the explicitly resolved Latin reading; it does not establish independent transmission or another printed edition.

The full printed conclusion supplies the punctuation exemplar Filium tuum: Qui tecum and Spiritus Sancti, Deus used in expanding the abbreviated Vigil collect. This is a formula exemplar, not another printing of the Vigil proper body.

The approved Benziger page prints the Vigil collect body and the abbreviated Per eundem Dominum. The full continuation and its punctuation are supported by the separately bound standard-conclusion rule and formula exemplar, not printed in full on this proper page.

locator.section: Rubricae generales Missalis romani, nn. 511 d, 513 a, 514.

entries.claim: The celebrant says or sings the collect and its conclusion.

The general rule supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion and its terminal Per omnia saecula saeculorum with Amen. This is the standard continuation of the abbreviation on the Vigil proper page, not a full local-page quotation.

RG 115 b gives Per eundem Dominum nostrum, etc. ut supra when an oration addressed to the Father mentions the Son at its beginning. The Vigil proper independently prints Per eúndem Dóminum after referring to the Lord’s Resurrection. The rule identifies that form; the Vigil text does not name the Son explicitly and supplies no eiusdem in the conclusion.
